we present a patient conceived through assisted reproductive technology who has pseudohypoparatyroidism type 2, and that we have found an association between assisted reproductive technology and imprinting disorders.

we describe a child with PHP1B conceived by ART, with an almost complete loss of methylation of the GNAS A/B exon, and an associated gain of methylation at the NESP55 exon, but without evidence for a microdeletion of the GNAS/ STX16 region or patUPD20q.
A patient with a methylation defect causing PHP1B was conceived by assisted conception, and that an increase in creatine kinase was associated with an increased in PTH concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether assisted reproductive technologies (IVF) are a risk factor for the development of imprinting defects in the human.
the following questions: What are the effects of ART on epigenetic regulation?
the possible role of assisted reproductive technologies in the development of imprinting disorders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report the first case of pseudohypoparityroidism type 2B associated with assisted reproduction technology.

a patient with a methylation defect that causes pseudohypoparatthyroidism type 2B, who was conceived by assisted reproductive techniques, had an increase creatine kinase level that was associated with an increased PTH concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high creatine kinase concentration may be associated with a PTH increase in children.
PHP1B is an imprinting disorder and should be included in the differential diagnosis of a child conceived by ART with a high creatine kinase level and an elevated PTH concentration.

the increased incidence of imprinter disorders in children conceived with assisted reproduction technology should not be underestimated and that the diagnosis of pseudohypoparatyroidism should be considered when an increased creatine kinase is associated with an elevated PTH level.
